summary: Enterprise security review: request for tenant-configurable retention controls + evidence of enforcement (audit logs, admin activity, telemetry)
environment: prod (N/A - security review request, no runtime impact)
description:
Request type: Enterprise security review / evidence request

Customer/prospect context:
- Prospect A is in procurement + security review for Hosted API with a near-term path to Dedicated.
- They have internal retention and eDiscovery requirements and are asking for configurable retention controls plus proof that enforcement is real (not policy-only).

Requested artifacts / questions (from customer questionnaire + call notes):
1) Retention configurability
   - Can retention be configured per tenant for:
     a) audit logs (user/admin actions)
     b) admin activity logs (Console actions, config changes)
     c) inference request metadata (timestamps, model, tokens, status; not raw prompts)
     d) telemetry/analytics (aggregated usage/cost/latency)
     e) operational logs (platform/service logs)
   - Need min/max bounds and ability to set 30/90/365 days depending on data type.

2) Proof of enforcement
   - Evidence that data is actually deleted or TTL’d, not just hidden.
   - Evidence that changes to retention policies are auditable.
   - Evidence of monitoring/alerts for enforcement failures.

3) Exports & SIEM
   - Audit log export format (CSV/JSON) and whether exports are constrained by retention.
   - Can they export to a SIEM and what metadata is included.

4) Exceptions / legal hold
   - Ability to apply legal hold to prevent deletion (eDiscovery), who can approve, and how it’s documented.

5) Timeline
   - They want a “current state” answer now for the security review, and a delivery plan for configurable retention controls.
   - Their procurement target: decision by 2025-03-01. If retention is not configurable by then, they request a contractual commitment + interim workaround.

What we can provide immediately (draft plan):
- Customer-ready baseline compliance reporting pack section on retention + audit logging coverage (sanitized, no sensitive internals).
- Current defaults and which datasets are eligible for retention enforcement in v1.
- Description of legal hold / exception workflow (process + role-based approvals).

Open items (need owners):
- Confirm exact v1 supported datasets for customer-facing statements.
- Confirm default retention values by product tier (Hosted vs Dedicated) that we are comfortable sharing.
- Confirm whether we can share screenshots of Console retention controls behind feature flag, or only narrative until GA.

Internal stakeholders:
- Product: Naomi Feldman (Security & Compliance), Marissa Cole (Console)
- Eng: Marcus Lin (Security Eng), Kevin Osei (Retention controls & exports), Logan Wright (Telemetry)
- GRC: Olga Petrov

Attachments requested by customer (to be delivered as a zip or PDF set):
- “Retention controls overview” (1-2 pages)
- “Audit log retention & exports summary” (1-2 pages)
- “Control-to-evidence mapping for retention + audit logging” (table)
- “Legal hold & retention exceptions process” (1 page)
- SOC 2 report (under NDA) or SOC 2 bridge letter if available

Next step requested by customer:
- Send artifacts by 2025-02-12 for security review committee meeting.
comments: 2025-02-05 09:18 PT — Markus Klein (Solutions Eng) — Created ticket from security review intake. Prospect’s security team is specifically pushing on “configurable retention per dataset” + “evidence of deletion.” They cited prior vendors who only had policy statements. They asked for screenshots or proof points (job logs, monitoring).

2025-02-05 11:02 PT — Rachel Kim (Enterprise Readiness) — Taking ownership. I’ll coordinate with Naomi/Olga for customer-facing pack, and with Kevin/Marcus for technical statements we can safely share. Goal: ship a clean response package (PDF) + a short email cover note by 02/12.

2025-02-06 13:40 PT — Naomi Feldman (Product, Sec/Compliance) — For “current state”: we should be explicit about what is configurable today vs roadmap. For v1 retention controls: we will support tenant-configurable retention for audit logs + selected admin activity + eligible analytics tables; not all operational logs. We should also define guardrails (min/max) and legal hold semantics. Please avoid implying we can retain raw inference payloads beyond current posture.

2025-02-07 10:25 PT — Olga Petrov (GRC) — I can provide a draft control-to-evidence matrix for retention + audit logging, but it needs review by Marcus for accuracy (what’s actually logged + where). We should include evidence examples: policy change audit event, retention enforcement job run record, and export metadata showing retention boundary warnings.

2025-02-07 15:05 PT — Kevin Osei (Security Eng) — Exporter behavior: exports will respect retention boundaries (no “resurrecting” expired events). For customers asking to export older events, answer should be: retention policy must be set accordingly prior to the timeframe; legal hold can prevent deletion where supported. Also note that export jobs emit metadata including export range, retention-effective window, and warnings if requested range extends beyond retention.

2025-02-10 09:30 PT — Rachel Kim — Draft customer package assembled (internal). Pending approvals: (1) final wording for default retention values by dataset, (2) whether we can include Console UI screenshots (feature-flagged). If screenshots are not permitted, we’ll include annotated mock/wireframe and state “UI subject to change; available in early access.”

2025-02-11 16:12 PT — Marcus Lin (Security Eng) — OK to include high-level enforcement description + monitoring stance (dashboards/alerts) but avoid sharing internal dashboard links/screenshots. We can provide: description of scheduled enforcement jobs, auditability (job run records), and that failures page SRE/on-call per standard. For legal hold: must be explicitly requested and approved; enforcement respects hold flags.

2025-02-12 08:55 PT — Rachel Kim — Sent email to customer with package v0.9 (Retention overview, Audit log retention/exports, Legal hold process, Control-to-evidence table). SOC 2 report will be provided under NDA via Trust portal workflow (separate thread). Asked customer to confirm (a) required retention windows per data type, and (b) whether they need tenant-level self-serve configuration at launch or if support-assisted configuration is acceptable for initial rollout.

2025-02-13 14:20 PT — Markus Klein — Customer replied: minimum retention requirements are 90 days for audit logs and admin activity; telemetry can be 30 days; they want ability to set 365 days for audit logs on request. Legal hold is required (case-by-case). They are OK with support-assisted configuration for first 60 days, but want self-serve in Console as part of enterprise readiness.

2025-02-18 10:05 PT — Rachel Kim — Updated response back to customer: confirmed our plan supports 30/90/365 day options with guardrails; self-serve Console controls are part of the roadmap (targeting staged rollout). Requested customer NDA completion for SOC2 report. Marking ticket Waiting on Customer for NDA + confirmation of which deployment mode they are pursuing first (Hosted vs Dedicated), as defaults and evidence package differ slightly.
internal_notes:

If customer asks for contractual retention commitments, loop in Sofia Mendes (commercial counsel) and Michael Grant (legal hold language) and reference procurement call notes.
